transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-21 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees (recorded): Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Evan Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Sunrise CTO), Lena Morales (Platform Engineer), Ibrahim Khan (Head of Data), Sophie Li (Security)

Auto-summary (auto generated, may be incomplete):
Sunrise is evaluating which deployment mode to use for a 3-month POC: hosted API for rapid iteration, dedicated reserved capacity for predictable latency/cost, or a private VPC/on-prem stack due to regulatory routing and occasional edge gateways. Success criteria discussed: P95 latency target, throughput burn rate, cost per 1M tokens, data residency, and audit logs. Action items focused on benchmarks, sample traffic, and security paperwork.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call — i see raj, lena, ibrahim, sophie — can you confirm?
[00:05] Raj: yep, this is raj — thanks. loud and clear.
[00:08] Lena: lena here. morning.
[00:12] Ibrahim: ibrahim — good to be here.
[00:14] Sophie: sophie joining from security.
[00:17] Maya: awesome. goal for the hour, map out POC success criteria and decide which hosting lane makes the most sense: hosted, dedicated, or private. evan will run through benchmarks and priya will note integration points.
[00:30] Evan: hey — quick context, i skimmed your prep notes. you have an edge device fleet that pre-processes messages and then forwards to a core service, correct?
[00:37] Raj: yes — roughly. we do light extraction at the edge and then call the core for heavier NLU and reranking. sometimes latency from edge to cloud spikes because of intermittent cellular.
[00:47] Evan: ok. so two patterns: low latency critical path for live routing decisions (~50-150ms target) and bulk async jobs for nightly reconciliation. POC should hit both.
[00:59] Lena: when you say 50-150ms, that's at P95 or end-to-end? we were thinking p95 end-to-end for the live path at peak shipments (~120 qps).
[01:10] Evan: good clarification — we typically measure P95 server-side. if end-to-end required, you add network from edge to region. for the POC we can provide both server-side P95 and estimated end-to-end with your edge numbers.
[01:22] Ibrahim: current baseline: internal heuristic model lives in k8s on gcp, p95 is about 340ms and cost is high — so we're trying to reduce latency and cost by 30-50%.
[01:33] Priya: and also we need deterministic performance for SLA reasons; some lanes of our app are regulated.
[01:39] Maya: ok let's talk tradeoffs. Hosted: fastest to start, no infra ops, easy for iteration. Dedicated: reserved GPUs in our dedicated pools gives more predictable throughput and lower per-token cost. Private: VPC/on-prem gives full control for compliance and data residency but higher setup time and ops overhead.
[01:57] Raj: two follow-ups — one, can dedicated handle bursty workloads? two, private: do you support routing from edge gateways into an on-prem inference cluster?
[02:10] Evan: dedicated supports configurable autoscaling plus burst capacity; you can set scaling policies. for edge routing, private deployments can be set up behind your gateway — we've done TLS mutual auth and an edge gateway pattern. there is some initial network work though.
[02:25] Sophie: for private we need KMS integration and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. we also need control-plane separation — can the control plane be in r/w model?
[02:35] Priya: control plane options vary — we offer a customer-managed private control plane pattern where API tokens and RBAC map to your idp. maya, maybe you want to speak to that?
[02:43] Maya: yes — for Private we ship a private control plane and optionally an on-prem package. KMS integration (bring-your-own) is supported; audit logs can be pushed to syslog or an S3-compatible endpoint. fine-grained RBAC and SSO/SAML are standard.
[02:58] Lena: great. some of our workloads have PII — we need retention controls and redact-before-store patterns. are logs redaction-ready?
[03:06] Evan: audit logs can be redacted at ingestion and we can configure token-level retention. note though there might be tradeoffs with observability detail when redaction is applied.
[03:18] Raj: let's nail success criteria for the POC. i'll propose: 1) server-side P95 <= 80ms for live path, 2) sustain 120 QPS with <5% error rate, 3) cost <= 40% of current per-inference spend for equivalent throughput, 4) validated security posture with SOC-like artifacts.
[03:38] Maya: concise — we'll add acceptance: model parity for quality (avs some gold prompts) and a rollout plan to production if POC meets criteria.
[03:46] Ibrahim: how long to get a hosted POC vs dedicated vs private up? timeline wise.
[03:50] Evan: hosted: we can do smoke tests in 48 hours, full workload benchmark in 1 week. dedicated: capacity reservation and cluster setup ~2-3 weeks. private: network and security review plus on-prem image deployment is 4-6 weeks depending on network schedules.
[04:04] Lena: ok that time delta matters. we have an internal business sprint end of june so earlier is preferred.
[04:09] Maya: so recommended route: start hosted to iterate quickly on prompts and integration, run a hosted benchmark to collect baseline, then move to a dedicated pilot for cost/stability tests. private only if compliance gating prevents hosted/dedicated.
[04:24] Raj: that seems sensible. a concern: tokens and model selection — do you have quantized variants? we want to evaluate cost with 8-bit fine-tuned variants if possible.
[04:34] Evan: yes we provide quantized model variants and performance profiles per model; we can include a 4-model sweep in the POC: base float, 8-bit q, 4-bit where available, and a smaller distilled model. we'll report latency, memory footprint, and subjective quality delta via prompt sets.
[04:51] Ibrahim: benchmark specifics — what harness do you need from our side? we'll give traffic shape but anything else?
[04:57] Evan: ideal: sample payloads (real-ish with sensitive data redacted), 7 days of qps histogram, representative prompt set for quality evals, and any custom pre/post processing you do at edge. we'll run mixed open-loop and closed-loop tests; open-loop for raw throughput, closed-loop for end-to-end latencies.
[05:15] Lena: for closed loop, add emulated network latencies to reflect cellular — we can share typical RTT percentiles. can you simulate that?
[05:22] Priya: yes we can add a network emulation layer in the harness.
[05:26] Sophie: security checklist — we need to confirm encryption in transit, at rest, KMS integration, SSO, audit retention period, and the ability to perform a security review / pen test.
[05:36] Maya: we'll share our security pack (SOC2, ISO artifacts) and a private connectivity checklist. we'll also note which items require private deployment (e.g., local-only KMS or air-gap).
[05:45] Raj: curious about cost modelling — what inputs do you need?
[05:48] Evan: tokens per request distribution, average tokens per conversation, session stickiness (KV cache reuse), and target QPS. we'll present a per-1M token cost for hosted and a committed-rate model for dedicated.
[06:00] Ibrahim: our session stickiness is high — about 70% of requests can reuse KV cache across a user session which should favor a caching-optimized runtime. can you expose cache hit rates in the dashboards?
[06:11] Priya: yes, we can surface token-level cache hits, per-route latency, and cost attribution in the console.
[06:18] Lena: on dedicated, do you allow model pinning per route so we can run A/B between quant levels?
[06:24] Evan: yes, rollout policies and model pinning are supported so you can route a percentage to a quantized variant and monitor quality regressions.
[06:30] Sophie: please also include information about audit log forwarding options and retention when you send the security docs.
[06:36] Maya: will do.
[06:38] Raj: what about cold-starts — gaussy startup when a GPU spins up — is that significant?
[06:42] Evan: there is a warm-up cost when kernels load and KV cache populates; we mitigate with continuous batching and pre-warming. dedicated reduces cold starts because you control reserved capacity; hosted can use burst pools but warmups still occur on scale events. we'll include cold-start metrics in the benchmark.
[06:58] Ibrahim: any examples of similar customers with edge-to-core patterns?
[07:01] Maya: we've done something similar with Meridian Bio (healthcare routing) and with Peregrine Logistics (shipping); i'll share anonymized notes and a benchmark deck.
[07:10] Raj: good. on compliance, if we need private, what's the minimum lead time? we heard 4-6 weeks but anything that can be parallelized?
[07:18] Evan: we can parallelize security review with image build and network config; if you frontload firewall rules and KMS details we can aim for 3 weeks but depends on interop with your infra team.
[07:29] Sophie: we'll assign a network engineer to work with you, that should speed it up.
[07:33] Lena: ok benchmarks: can we make a short list of tests you will run and the metrics?
[07:37] Evan: yes — proposed benchmark suite:
 - open-loop throughput (QPS by model variant),
 - closed-loop P95 latency under 120 QPS with edge latency emulation,
 - cold-start time to first token under scale events,
 - model-quality sweep (NDCG/accuracy on supplied prompt set),
 - token-cost per 1M tokens calculation (hosted vs dedicated committed),
 - cache hit rate and per-route cost allocation.
[08:05] Raj: sounds thorough. for acceptance we'll expect a benchmark report and a quick demo of the monitoring console.
[08:12] Maya: yep we'll produce a report and a dashboard link for the POC.
[08:15] Ibrahim: what about data deletion in hosted — do you support immediate purge?
[08:19] Evan: we have retention controls; for hosted we provide configurable retention windows and can support purge requests — in some cases, cold storage logs may take longer to scrub, we'll specify timelines in the security pack.
[08:30] Sophie: are you able to provide an SLA for dedicated? we need an SLA-backed latency target for production moves.
[08:36] Maya: dedicated comes with an SLA for uptime and a latency SLO commitment depending on reserved config — we'll include sample SLO language in the pricing pack.
[08:45] Raj: ok let's talk cost roughly now — assume 120 QPS, avg tokens 45 per request, say 5M tokens/day — can you give an order of magnitude?
[08:56] Evan: rough rough: hosted per-1M tokens X dollars (we'll put numbers in the spreadsheet), dedicated commit often brings unit cost down 20-50% depending on utilization and batchability, private cost depends on infra and licensing. we'll send a sample calc with your numbers.
[09:12] Lena: please note we prefer per-route cost visibility — we want to isolate the live routing cost from batch reconciliation.
[09:18] Priya: console supports per-route cost and token breakdown.
[09:21] Raj: final things — timeline alignment: we want a hosted benchmark by May 1 to inform sprint decision. can you meet that?
[09:28] Maya: yes — action: we will aim to run hosted smoke + benchmark by 2026-05-01 if we get traffic shape and prompt set by 2026-04-23.
[09:35] Raj: agreed. any blockers?
[09:38] Sophie: security wants the pack and a preliminary network checklist — i'll review and flag show-stoppers.
[09:43] Maya: we'll share the security pack and dedicated/private checklist after this call. evan will draft benchmark plan.
[09:50] Evan: i'll put the benchmark plan in a shared doc and propose two test windows next week.
[09:54] Lena: also please include notes about KV cache tuning — we have long sessions so that may be key for cost.
[09:59] Evan: noted.
[10:02] Raj: great. appreciate the clarity.
[10:05] Maya: recap of next steps then — (1) sunrse provides traffic + prompt set by 2026-04-23, (2) redwood shares hosting vs dedicated cost spreadsheet by 2026-04-24, (3) evan shares benchmark plan by 2026-04-22, (4) schedule connectivity/security sync by 2026-04-27.
[10:22] Ibrahim: sounds good. thanks all.
[10:24] Sophie: thanks.
[10:25] Maya: thanks everyone — we'll send notes and the security pack. bye.

End of transcript.
